subject: Proposal: Prohibit model learning & exportability clauses for ClearPulse
messages:
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia@clearpulsehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Berger <tberger@clearpulsehealth.com>, legal@clearpulsehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-18T09:34:00-08:00
Subject: Initial ask: learning prohibition + EU residency for ClearPulse

Hi Hannah –

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement & legal have a couple of non-negotiables we need for any pilot that will see PHI-derived prompts and responses:

- A firm prohibition on using our data to improve models or otherwise train (we need contractual language that prohibits "learning from customer content" and a process for attestations).
- Exportability controls: logs and any model-derived artifacts must not be used or exported outside the US without explicit approval.
- Prompt/response ownership: ClearPulse needs explicit rights to request prompt/response exports and retain copies; we need clarity that Redwood won’t assert derivative rights.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to these points in the DPA, and what evidence you can provide (subprocessor list, SOC2 reports, retention settings)? I’ve attached our standard DPA template.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Ramos
Sr. Procurement Manager | ClearPulse Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@clearpulsehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T12:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: learning prohibition + EU residency for ClearPulse

Hi Alicia —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front: yes, we can contractually prohibit model learning from ClearPulse traffic, and we can set up an architecture & operational controls to satisfy the export/residency requirements for the pilot. A few details and trade-offs below so legal can pick language that matches expectations.

What we propose for the DPA (high level):
- Prohibit model improvement: Redwood will not use ClearPulse content to train, fine-tune, or improve base models or any model variants used to serve the account (we can add explicit prohibition language and audit controls).
- Isolation mode: we provide a "non-learning" serving mode which disables telemetry ingestion for model improvement, enforces strict logs retention, and routes traffic to a restricted inference pool.
- Subprocessor & export controls: we’ll include an auditable subprocessor inventory (attached snapshot) and an export restriction clause that requires Redwood to obtain written customer approval before transferring any customer-derived artifacts outside the US.
- Prompt/response access & IP: we will not claim ownership over prompts/responses. We can add a clause clarifying that Redwood’s only rights are to provide the service, and that derivatives created solely from ClearPulse content are not Redwood-owned.

Operational evidence we can provide immediately:
- Latest subprocessor snapshot (attached).
- SOC 2 Type II summary and available control mappings (can share under NDA).
- A short runbook describing how the non-learning serving mode is enforced and how we attest to it.

Two practical notes:
1) For complete isolation (no chance of leakage into global model improvement pipelines) we recommend the Dedicated offering or a private tenancy. Hosted non-learning mode reduces model improvement risk but for some customers Dedicated is the stronger contractual guarantee.
2) There’s an incremental fee for the operational overhead of non-learning routing and for granular export controls. We can scope that in the SOW.

I’ve redlined your DPA template and attached a starting PDF with the proposed language called "ClearPulse_DPA_redline_v1.pdf". Can you confirm if ClearPulse legal wants the Dedicated path or if you want to attempt the hosted non-learning pilot first?

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Trust & Security | Redwood Inference

From: Tom Berger <tberger@clearpulsehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Alicia Ramos <alicia@clearpulsehealth.com>
Cc: legal@clearpulsehealth.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: learning prohibition + EU residency for ClearPulse

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick reply and the redline. A couple follow-ups from procurement:
- Can Redwood provide a per-route flag we can toggle to ensure specific API keys are always in non-learning mode? We'd prefer that to account-level toggles so some integrations can still use learning if we authorize them later.
- On attestations: procurement needs a quarterly attestation we can use for audits confirming no learning occurred for the flagged keys.

Legal will want tighter language around "derivative" — they insist on the ability to export model artifacts created from our prompts (e.g., fine-grained conversation logs plus extracted knowledge artifacts) and want confirmation Redwood won’t assert derivative IP.

Also, before we trade redlines in earnest, legal will want to see your subprocessor CSV and a pointer to the SOC2, plus the contact for security for a short call.

Tom

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Berger <tberger@clearpulsehealth.com>, Alicia Ramos <alicia@clearpulsehealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T11:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: learning prohibition + EU residency for ClearPulse

Tom / Alicia —

Quick technical clarifications that will inform contract language:
- Per-route non-learning flag: yes, we support per-API-key routing to a non-learning pool. It’s implemented as metadata on the API key and enforced at the routing layer; keys marked non-learning never feed downstream model improvement pipelines.
- Quarterly attestation: we can provide an attestation (signed by our Security and Compliance leads) that lists keys in non-learning mode and the checks we ran. We can include a hash of sample logs to demonstrate integrity without sharing customer content.
- Artifacts & derivatives: when you say "export model artifacts created from our prompts" — operationally we can provide conversation logs, enriched transcripts, and extracted entities. If you want model weights or anything that implies retraining a model on your data, that would be covered by the non-learning prohibition. The DPA language should separate (a) customer data exports (which we can provide on request) from (b) model weights/derived models (which Redwood will not produce from your data if covered by the prohibition).

Attached is our latest subprocessor snapshot (redwood_subprocessors_snapshot_20261117.csv) for your review. Please flag any vendors you want called out for additional controls.

If this matches your expectations we can draft a short SOW for the pilot (non-learning per-key routing, attestation cadence, and the export-approval workflow).

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Product – Security Controls | Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Ramos <alicia@clearpulsehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Berger <tberger@clearpulsehealth.com>, legal@clearpulsehealth.com, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: learning prohibition + EU residency for ClearPulse

Thanks all — this is helpful. Legal reviewed the redline and will loop in a couple of minor wording requests (we want the export approval to be "written and time-bound" and the attestation to include the attestor's title). We also want the ability to request an on-site audit if we move to Dedicated later.

For now procurement is comfortable proceeding with a hosted pilot using per-key non-learning flags, plus the quarterly attestation and the export-approval workflow you described. Please send a draft SOW and updated DPA language with the export approval clause set to require explicit written consent (with a 30-day approval window).

We accepted the redlined DPA as a starting point and uploaded a signed acknowledgement to the HubSpot deal (link below). Please let us know next steps for the SOW and an intro to security so legal can finish the SOC2 review.

Thanks,
Alicia

Attachments referenced: ClearPulse_DPA_redline_v1.pdf (redlined DPA), redwood_subprocessors_snapshot_20261117.csv
